title: Four weeks until Dana leaves
scenario: A startup is moving its support assistant from prototype to production on the Claude API. The company has a zero data retention (ZDR) arrangement with Anthropic. A reviewer lists four findings (exhibit). You decide the fix for each.
exhibit:
(made-up example data)

PRODUCTION REVIEW, support assistant

  1. KEYS      Production uses a personal API key created by Dana.
               Dana leaves the company in 4 weeks.

  2. BROWSER   The web app calls the Claude API directly.
               The key is inside the front-end JavaScript bundle.

  3. LEAK      A test script printed a key in a public CI log:
               sk-ant-EXAMPLE-not-a-real-key
               The key is still active.

  4. DATA      Legal rule: no customer content stored at the vendor
               after the response.
               Plan: a nightly summary job on the Message Batches API.

questions.prompt: Finding 1: what happens when Dana leaves, and what is the fix?

options.text: Nothing. API keys belong to the organization, so they keep working.
options.explanation: A personal key acts as one user. Claude archives personal keys when that user is removed from the organization.

options.text: Ask Dana to set the key's expiry to Never just before leaving.
options.explanation: Expiry is not the issue. The key stops when its owner is removed, whatever its expiry says.

options.text: It stops working. Use a service account key from a secrets manager.
options.explanation: Right. Claude says shared or production workloads should use a service account, which has its own identity.

options.text: Copy the key into a shared .env file in the repo so it stays.
options.explanation: That puts a secret in version control, which is the opposite of the docs' advice to use a secrets manager.

questions.prompt: Finding 3: a live key is in a public CI log. What should the team do now?

options.text: Disable or delete the key, deploy a replacement, check usage.
options.explanation: Right. A leaked key must be dead before anything else. Claude's Usage API can filter by API key to look for misuse.

options.text: Edit the CI log to remove the key, and keep using the same key.
options.explanation: The key was already public, and others may have copied it. Editing the log does not make it safe.

options.text: Give the key a 3-hour expiry so it ends by itself later today.
options.explanation: Claude sets an expiry only when a key is created. It cannot be changed afterward.

options.text: Watch usage for a day and revoke only if something looks odd.
options.explanation: OpenAI says to revoke a compromised key promptly. Waiting leaves a public key open to anyone.

questions.prompt: Finding 4: can the nightly job run on the Message Batches API under the legal rule?

options.text: Yes, because the API blocks any feature that would break ZDR.
options.explanation: Claude says that under ZDR the API does not block features marked No. Using one steps outside ZDR.

options.text: No, Batch is not ZDR eligible, so use the standard Messages API.
options.explanation: Right. Claude lists Batch as not ZDR eligible, with 29-day retention. The nightly job should run on the standard API, within rate limits.

options.text: Yes, because ZDR covers only Claude Code and not API calls.
options.explanation: ZDR covers the Messages and Token Counting APIs for eligible features. Batch is the exception here.

options.text: Yes, because batch data is deleted after 24 hours on both vendors.
options.explanation: Claude keeps batch data for up to 29 days after creation. OpenAI also marks its batch endpoint as not ZDR eligible.

questions.prompt: Finding 2: the browser calls the API with the key in the bundle. What is the fix?

options.text: Minify the bundle so the key is hard to read.
options.explanation: Anyone can read network requests in the browser. A hidden key is still public.

options.text: Give every user their own key in the browser.
options.explanation: That puts many secrets in many browsers and makes limits and cost harder to control.

options.text: Rotate the key every day and leave it in the bundle.
options.explanation: Rotation shortens the exposure, but the key is still public to every visitor in the meantime.

options.text: Call your own server, which holds the key.
options.explanation: Right. The server keeps the key, authenticates the user, applies a per-user limit and can send a hashed user id (OpenAI calls this safety_identifier).
